FAQ
Questions about getting started.
What's the difference between Builder and the other MFFU plans?

Builder is the easiest path to funding in the prop space and the only MFFU plan with a fixed payout ladder to live capital — five rungs, each up to $2,000, then a real brokerage account. It has a one-day minimum evaluation, a $1,000 soft-pause daily loss limit, and an 80/20 split. Rapid pays daily on sim with a 90/10 split and no fixed ladder. Pro has the highest payout cap at $100K and its own path to live.

How does the Builder payout ladder actually work?

After you pass the evaluation, you trade a sim-funded Builder account through up to five approved payout cycles. Before your first payout, you need to clear the required buffer — $2,100 on the default plan, $1,600 on the add-on. Once the buffer is cleared, each payout cycle requires a minimum of 2 qualifying trading days, at least $500 net profit since your last payout, and must fall between $500 and $2,000. A 50% consistency rule applies at the payout stage — your single best day can't account for more than half of that cycle's profits. After your fifth approved sim payout, you graduate to a live brokerage account at Blue Row Capital with daily payouts, an 80/20 split, and no consistency rule.

What is a "soft pause" daily loss limit?

When your session hits $1,000 down for the day, trading pauses until the next session — but the account is not breached. It is a coaching mechanism for traders still building discipline, not a hard kill switch. You return the next day with the account intact.

When do I graduate from sim funded to live on Builder?

After five approved sim payouts on your Builder account. The fifth approved payout triggers promotion to a live account underwritten by Blue Row Capital.

Can I have more than one Builder account at the same time?

No. Builder is limited to one active Builder account per user. The plan is built for focus, not for stacking multiple evals.

What happens if I breach on Builder?

If you breach max drawdown on the sim-funded Builder account, the account ends and you start a new evaluation. Hitting the $1,000 daily soft-pause limit only ends your session for that day — it does not breach the account. Note: if you breach after graduating to a live account at Blue Row Capital, a 21-day cooldown applies — no sim funded trading, no new eval purchases, and no resets during that period.

Is Builder good for beginners?

Yes — Builder is designed as the easiest entry path to MFFU with forgiving EOD trailing drawdown, a one-day pass minimum, and a clear five-payout path to live capital. The soft-pause daily loss limit gives traders room to learn without a single bad session ending the account.

How is Builder different from other low-cost one-step plans?

Most low-cost one-step plans stop at sim. Builder includes a documented five-payout ladder to a real live brokerage seat, $0 activation fee, EOD trailing drawdown (not intraday), and a soft-pause DLL that keeps the account alive after a bad day.

What does the live Builder account look like?

After five approved sim payouts, you trade live capital at Blue Row Capital. The live account carries an EOD trailing drawdown of $2,000 (default plan) or $1,500 (add-on plan), which becomes static once the MLL reaches $0. You get daily payouts, an 80/20 split, a $1,000 daily loss limit, no consistency rule, and one live account per user. A 21-day cooldown applies if the live account is breached.

You keep 90% of every payout. MFFU keeps 10%. There's no graduated tier, no 'first $X at one rate, then a different rate.' Every payout you request on a Rapid account follows the same 90/10 split.

How fast can I get my first payout on Rapid?

The evaluation requires two trading days. Once funded, you need to build the required buffer ($2,100 on the $50K account) in realized profits before your first payout request. After that threshold is cleared, you can request every 24 hours. For most traders, first payout eligibility comes a few days into the funded stage — it depends entirely on how quickly you build the buffer.

What is intraday trailing drawdown?

Intraday trailing drawdown means your max-loss floor moves up with your equity in real time during the session — not just at end-of-day. On Rapid Sim Funded, once your balance is +$100 above your starting balance after your first payout, the floor locks and stops trailing upward permanently.

Does the Rapid plan have a daily loss limit?

No. Rapid has no daily loss limit in either the evaluation or the funded stage. The only loss constraint is your max drawdown — that's it.

What's the difference between Rapid and the other MFFU plans?

Rapid is built for speed: daily payouts, 2-day pass, 90/10 split, $0 activation fee. Builder is the low-cost entry plan with a structured 5-payout ladder to a live brokerage seat. Pro has the largest account sizes and highest per-payout cap. Flex is a separate plan available in $25K and $50K sizes — it has different payout mechanics. Rapid is the plan MFFU recommends for traders who want the fastest payout cadence and best profit split.

Is there an activation fee on Rapid?

No. Rapid has zero activation fees at every account size. When you pass the evaluation, your funded account activates instantly — you don't pay anything additional to unlock it.

Can I hold positions overnight on Rapid?

No. Rapid is intended for intraday futures trading. All positions must be closed before the daily session close. Holding overnight will breach the account.

What happens if I hit the max loss on Rapid?

On a Rapid Evaluation, breaching the max drawdown fails that evaluation, but you can reset it for a specific fee and start trading again. On a Rapid Sim Funded account, breaching the max drawdown closes the account. Funded accounts can't be reset, so you'll need to start a new evaluation. The max drawdown is a hard line, so we recommend trading well above it.

Why is Tier 1 news trading restricted on Rapid?

Tier 1 news events (CPI, NFP, FOMC, etc.) create extreme short-term volatility that can blow out simulated accounts before stop-losses fill. To keep the simulated market behavior representative of live execution risk, T1 events are restricted within 2 minutes before and after the release.

How many Rapid accounts can I have at the same time?

For $25K and $50K Rapid accounts, you can hold up to five active sim funded accounts at once. For $100K and $150K accounts, the limit is three total sim funded accounts across all plans.

FAQ
Questions about the Pro plan.
What's the difference between Pro and Rapid?

Rapid is available in four sizes ($25K–$150K) and pays daily on sim with a 90/10 split using intraday trailing drawdown. Pro starts at $50K, goes up to $150K, pays on a 14-day cycle with a $100,000 cap, uses EOD trailing drawdown, and has a defined path to live capital. Rapid is built for speed and cadence. Pro is built for scale and the live transition.

How does the Pro live transition actually work?

There are three ways a Pro account can transition to live. The most common is three consecutive payouts on the same account — after which the account is reviewed by our Risk Team. The second is profits exceeding the $100,000 payout cap, where the excess is transitioned to a live balance, up to the maximum allowed by the account size, rather than paid out. The third is a proactive outreach from the Risk Team at any point during your sim funded journey based on your performance. Approved traders move to a real brokerage account at Blue Row Capital — real money, daily payouts, and an 80/20 split. Note: live account parameters differ from sim funded, including a daily loss limit, reduced contract limits, and a static drawdown floor. The trigger is documented; the review is human.

Why is there a 14-day payout window on Pro?

The 14-day window runs from your first trade on the sim funded account. It gives the EOD trailing drawdown time to settle toward a stable floor and establishes an equity track record before your first payout request. You also need to have cleared the required buffer before a payout can be approved — so the practical unlock is whichever comes later: 14 calendar days or buffer cleared.

What's the max payout I can actually withdraw on Pro per cycle?

Up to $100,000 per cycle, subject to your live equity above the required buffer at the time of request. Most competing "pro" tiers cap each cycle at $5,000 or 50% of account balance — Pro is the cap that doesn't become the binding constraint in your best months.

What is Blue Row Capital and how do I get there?

Blue Row Capital is the live brokerage relationship MFFU traders graduate into. Once your Pro account hits three consecutive payouts and clears risk-team review, your account is transitioned to a Blue Row Capital live brokerage seat — same rules, real money, real broker.

Is the Pro plan worth the cost over the Rapid plan?

It's worth it if you're optimizing for scale over cadence. Rapid is the better economic choice for active traders who want daily cashflow at a 90/10 split on smaller sizes. Pro is the better choice if you want a single account with up to $100K per payout, $50K–$150K sizes, no daily loss limit once funded, and a defined live transition.

How is the drawdown calculated on Pro?

Pro uses end-of-day trailing drawdown in both eval and sim funded. The max-loss line trails your equity high at the end of each trading day — not intraday. After your first approved payout, the MLL locks permanently at your starting balance plus $100 and stops trailing entirely. Until that first payout, the MLL continues to trail each time you set a new EOD equity high.

Does the Pro plan have a consistency rule?

There's a 50% consistency rule in evaluation only — no single day's profit can exceed 50% of your total eval profits. Once you're funded, there is no hard consistency rule. That said, the Pro plan does carry a Consistent Trading Policy: MFFU monitors sim funded accounts for trading behavior that falls outside professional norms — things like maxing contracts on every trade, contract flipping, inconsistent position sizing, or high-frequency strategies not aligned with your stated approach. Violations can result in restrictions or account termination. Trade like a professional and it won't be an issue.

What's the difference between EOD trailing and intraday trailing drawdown?

Intraday trailing (used by Rapid) updates the trailing max-loss line in real time as your equity moves up during the session — your highest unrealized P&L can pull the floor up against you. EOD trailing (used by Pro) only updates the line at the end of each trading day, based on your closing balance. EOD is the model used at most live brokerage seats, and it's more forgiving of mid-session volatility.

This Notice is not an employment contract or offer.

This Notice explains the manner in which MFFU collects, uses, and maintains nonpublic personal information about job applicants, including job applicants based in the United Kingdom ("UK"), the European Union ("EU"), or the European Economic Area ("EEA") as required under the General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 ("GDPR") or the GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018, as applicable.

Applicant means an individual who has applied for employment or an internship with MFFU.

Consent means any freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous indication of your wishes, by which you, by a clear affirmative action, signify agreement to the Processing of your Personal Data.

Process means any operation or set of operations which is performed on Personal Data, whether or not by automated means, including accessing, retrieving, collecting, recording, organizing, structuring, storing, adapting or altering, consulting, modifying, using, disclosing by transmission, transferring, disseminating or otherwise making it available, aligning or combining, restricting, erasing or destroying.

COOKIE POLICY - MY FUNDED FUTURES

1. Overview

MyFunded Futures, LLC, together with its affiliates ("MFFU," "we," "us," or "our"), wants you to be familiar with how we collect, use, and disclose information from and about you through cookies and similar technologies, because we respect your concerns about privacy and want to maintain your trust. We and our service providers and partners collect information by automated means when you visit, access, or use our website located at https://www.myfundedfutures.com/, together with our related mobile sites, applications, electronic newsletters, and widgets that link to this Cookie Policy (collectively, the "Services").

We are committed to responsible data practices and handle visitor data with the care described in this Policy. We do not use cookies to collect more personal information than necessary for the purposes described in this Policy.

This Cookie Policy should be read together with our Privacy Policy, which is available at https://www.myfundedfutures.com/privacy-policy, and which describes more fully how we collect, use, and disclose personal information, your rights and choices, and how to contact us.

2. What Are Cookies and Similar Technologies?

Cookies are small text files that are placed on your device when you visit a website. We and our service providers and partners use cookies and other tracking technologies, including web beacons, pixels, web server logs, software development kits (SDKs), JavaScript, and similar technologies (collectively, "Cookies"), to operate, secure, and improve the Services, to remember your preferences, to analyze how the Services are used, and to deliver and measure content and advertising.

The information we obtain through the use of Cookies may include information about your computer, device, and browser, such as your IP address, browser type, operating system and device characteristics, language preferences, mobile device identifier, referring URLs, and actions taken by you on the Services (such as the content you viewed, whether you have used the Services before, and the dates and times you access the Services). If you access the Services from a mobile or other device, we may collect a unique device identifier, geolocation data obtained with your consent where required by applicable law, and details about your mobile carrier.

First-party Cookies are set by MFFU. Third-party Cookies are set by parties other than MFFU, such as analytics and advertising partners, and are governed by those parties' own privacy and cookie notices. Cookies may be session Cookies (which expire when you close your browser) or persistent Cookies (which remain on your device until they expire or you delete them).

3. Categories of Cookies We Use

We use the following categories of Cookies on the Services. Depending on your jurisdiction and your choices, some of these Cookies may not be active during your visit.

Strictly Necessary Cookies. These Cookies are required to operate the Services and to provide features you have requested, such as login sessions, account security, evaluation dashboard access, page navigation, network management, and form submissions. The Services cannot function properly without these Cookies. These Cookies are always active and do not require your consent.

Functionality Cookies. These Cookies allow the Services to remember choices you make (such as your language, region, and content preferences) and to provide enhanced, more personalized features. These Cookies are placed subject to your consent where required by applicable law.

Analytics and Performance Cookies. These Cookies collect information about how visitors use the Services, including which pages are visited most often and whether users encounter errors, so that we can measure and improve the performance of the Services. This information is generally aggregated. Analytics providers we use include Google Analytics and HubSpot. See Section 6 for provider-specific opt-out options. These Cookies are placed subject to your consent where required by applicable law.

Advertising and Targeting Cookies. These Cookies are used by us and our advertising partners to deliver content and advertising that may be more relevant to you, including advertising relating to our simulated trading evaluations, to limit the number of times you see an advertisement, to measure the effectiveness of advertising campaigns, and to support cross-context behavioral advertising on and off the Services. These Cookies are placed subject to your consent where required by applicable law.

Social Networking Cookies. These Cookies enable you to share content from the Services through social networks and may be set by those social networks to track your activity across websites. They are governed by the relevant social network's own privacy and cookie notices. These Cookies are placed subject to your consent where required by applicable law.

4. Why We Use Cookies

We and our service providers and partners use Cookies to:

Operate, deliver, and secure the Services, and enable core functionality;
Remember your settings and preferences and recognize you when you return;
Understand and analyze how visitors use the Services and improve their performance, content, and design;
Deliver, personalize, and measure content and advertising, including cross-context behavioral advertising on and off the Services; and
Detect, prevent, and investigate fraud, abuse, and security incidents.
5. Third-Party Cookies

We use third-party service providers and advertising partners that may set cookies on our website in connection with analytics, marketing, advertising, and customer relationship management. The identity of these third parties may change over time as we engage new service providers, and this Policy will be updated to reflect material changes. For information about our current third-party partners' data practices, please refer to their respective privacy policies, which are accessible through the cookie consent tool on our website.

Third-party cookies set on our website may be used to support the following activities:

Anonymous visitor tracking. Prior to a visitor submitting any form on our website, a third party may assign a persistent, anonymous identifier to track browsing behavior across visits. This data is not linked to any personal information at this stage.

Contact identification and retroactive association. When a visitor submits a form or otherwise provides their contact information (such as when registering for or purchasing an evaluation), the applicable third party may associate that visitor's prior anonymous browsing history with their contact record. At this point, previously anonymous browsing data may become associated with an identifiable individual.

Marketing personalization and campaign tracking. Third parties may use cookies to track interactions with our email communications (such as opens and clicks), to personalize content on return visits, and to measure campaign performance, including tracking which pages a known contact visits after engaging with our communications.

Remarketing and behavioral advertising. We and our advertising partners may use cookies to serve advertisements to visitors on third-party platforms based on prior visits to our website, and to tailor the content and messaging displayed to visitors based on their browsing behavior and interactions with our Services.

Web analytics. We and our service providers use analytics tools to collect aggregated and individual-level data about how visitors interact with our website, including pages visited, session duration, traffic sources, and general geographic region. This data is used for internal analytics, website improvement, and marketing optimization purposes. Where technically available, we configure these services to anonymize IP addresses prior to storage.

Data collected through the Services may be processed and stored on servers located in the United States or other countries outside your jurisdiction. We rely on our third-party service providers' own data transfer mechanisms, which may include the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, standard contractual clauses, or other appropriate safeguards recognized under applicable law. We encourage EEA and UK visitors to review the privacy policies of our third-party service providers for further information about how they handle international data transfers.

For EU and UK visitors, where required by applicable law, we will only deploy analytics, marketing, or advertising cookies with your prior explicit consent, which may be withdrawn at any time.

MFFU may also set its own first-party cookies to support on-site personalization, targeted messaging, and marketing activities, including displaying tailored banners, content, and communications based on your browsing behavior and interactions with our Services. Where required by applicable law, such cookies will only be placed with your prior consent.

6. Your Choices and How to Manage Cookies

You have a number of ways to control or limit how we and our partners use Cookies. Please note that strictly necessary Cookies cannot be disabled because they are required for the Services to function.

Cookie Preferences Tool

Where required by applicable law, we will ask for your consent before placing non-essential Cookies on your device. You may accept, reject, or manage non-essential Cookies through the consent banner presented when you first access the Services, which is managed through HubSpot's cookie consent infrastructure. HubSpot's data practices are governed by HubSpot's own privacy policy. You may change your preferences at any time using the "Cookie Preferences" or "Cookie Settings" link on our website.

Manage my Cookie Preferences

Advertising and Cross-Context Behavioral Advertising

Where we and our partners use advertising Cookies for cross-context behavioral advertising, these activities may be considered a "sale" or "sharing" of personal information under certain U.S. state privacy laws. You may opt out of these activities by adjusting your preferences through the cookie consent banner on our website (labeled "Cookie Preferences" or "Cookie Settings"), or by broadcasting a recognized opt-out preference signal (such as the Global Privacy Control) through your browser. We honor recognized opt-out preference signals where required by applicable law.

Industry Opt-Out Tools

You may also opt out of interest-based advertising from participating companies through the Digital Advertising Alliance at optout.aboutads.info, the Network Advertising Initiative at optout.networkadvertising.org, and, for users in the EEA and UK, the European Interactive Digital Advertising Alliance at youronlinechoices.eu.

Browser Controls

Most web browsers allow you to control Cookies through their settings, typically found under the "Help," "Settings," or "Privacy" menu, including options to block or delete Cookies and to receive notification when a Cookie is set. For information about controlling Cookies through your specific browser, please visit the browser developer's website. If you disable or delete certain Cookies, some features of the Services may not function properly.

Analytics Opt-Out

The Services use analytics platforms that offer the opt-out mechanisms described below.

Google Analytics. We use Google Analytics to measure traffic and usage patterns. Google Analytics sets cookies including _ga, _gid, and _gat that collect information about how you interact with the Services. You may opt out by installing the browser add-on at tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout. For more information: policies.google.com/privacy.

HubSpot. We use HubSpot for marketing automation, contact management, and analytics. HubSpot sets persistent cookies including hubspotutk (tracks visitor identity across sessions and is passed to HubSpot on form submission), __hstc (tracks visitors across sessions), __hssc (tracks sessions), and __hs_opt_out (records your cookie opt-out preference). You may opt out via the "Cookie Preferences" tool on the Services or at legal.hubspot.com/privacy-policy.

California and Other U.S. State Residents

Residents of California and certain other U.S. states may have additional rights regarding personal information collected through cookies, including the right to opt out of the sale or sharing of personal information for cross-context behavioral advertising purposes. You may exercise these rights through the cookie consent banner on our website or by broadcasting a recognized opt-out preference signal (such as the Global Privacy Control) through your browser. For more information about your privacy rights, please refer to our Privacy Policy.

7. Do Not Track

Some browsers offer a "Do Not Track" (DNT) signal. Because no common industry standard for DNT has been adopted, the Services do not currently respond to DNT signals. We do, however, honor recognized opt-out preference signals (such as the Global Privacy Control) where required by applicable law, as described in Section 6.

8. Changes to this Cookie Policy

We reserve the right, at any time, to modify, alter, or update this Cookie Policy. Any such changes will be effective upon our posting of the revised Cookie Policy. Your continued use of the Services following our posting of any revised Cookie Policy will constitute your acknowledgement of the amended Cookie Policy. Please check this Cookie Policy periodically to remain informed of our practices. The latest version will always be available on our website, effective as of the date of posting.

9. Contact Information

If you have any questions about this Cookie Policy or our use of Cookies, please contact support@myfundedfutures.com.
